title: A peacock's train isn't its tail

scenes.headline: It's a train of upper tail coverts
scenes.body: The long eyespot feathers grow from above the tail. The real tail is shorter, behind them.

scenes.label: average 'train-rattling' shake
scenes.body: His real tail feathers strum the train about 26 times a second.

scenes.label: average train length
scenes.body: Shed each year and regrown before the breeding season.

caption:
The most famous 'tail' in India isn't a tail.

High-speed video showed the feather array resonates at the same frequencies peacocks use to rattle it, so the shake costs less energy.

Source: Dakin et al. 2016, PLOS ONE; Animal Diversity Web. Photos/video: Wikimedia Commons (credits on screen).
notes: Our core style: designed facts layered on one clip, each scene adds a new number. Original because the overlay carries peer-reviewed information the footage alone doesn't.
